claims.text: Power BI is Microsoft's business analytics platform for turning data into insights, and it operates as one of the core workloads of Microsoft Fabric, supplying the platform's analytics and visualization layer.

Power BI's main components are Power BI Desktop (a Windows authoring app for data modeling and report design), the cloud-based Power BI service (publishing, sharing, collaboration), and mobile apps for consuming reports on phones and tablets.

Existing Power BI content and workspaces carry into Microsoft Fabric without migration; users sign in with their existing Power BI or Microsoft 365 accounts and the Power BI interface stays familiar while Fabric layers on additional capabilities.

Within Fabric, Power BI shares platform-level features with other workloads — OneLake integration, Direct Lake mode, Dataflows Gen2 and notebooks, Purview-based security and governance, Data Activator alerting, and Copilot — while Desktop, the service, paginated reports, the visuals marketplace, Q&A, and goals/scorecards remain Power BI-specific.
Direct Lake mode, available to Power BI through Fabric, lets reports query data sitting in OneLake directly, without importing it into the model or maintaining a separate cache.
The recommended division of labor is to author and model in Power BI Desktop, then publish to the Power BI service for team sharing and collaboration, and use the mobile apps for on-the-go viewing.

Power BI Desktop connects to more than 100 data source types, transforms data with Power Query Editor, models with DAX (measures, calculated columns, relationships), offers 30+ built-in and custom visuals, and includes advanced tooling such as the performance analyzer, external tools, and composite models.

The Power BI service adds collaboration and operations capabilities on top of authored content: workspaces, apps for distributing dashboards and reports, dataflows for reusable data prep, shared datasets across reports, scheduled refresh, email subscriptions, alerts, Q&A natural-language queries, embedding, and data export.
The Power BI service implements security and oversight through row-level security (RLS), sensitivity labels, usage metrics, and audit logs.
Paginated reports, built with Power BI Report Builder, target structured pixel-perfect printable output such as invoices, complementing the interactive report format.
Organizations that must keep reporting on-premises can use Power BI Report Server and retain the option to move to the cloud later, rather than building a parallel reporting stack.
